entry.title: Killing random motions with finite velocity
entry.summary: In this paper, we study finite-velocity random motions subject to a killing mechanism acting at direction changes: at each change of direction, the motion is killed with a fixed probability and remains at its current position thereafter. We first consider the one-dimensional case of a standard telegraph process. We derive the exact distribution of the position at the killing time and show that it is Laplace distributed. We also characterize the law of the process conditional on survival up to a fixed time, proving that it coincides with that of a standard telegraph process driven by a thinned Poisson process with reduced switching intensity. We further derive the full time-dependent distribution of the killed process, including both its absolutely continuous and singular components. We then extend the analysis to a planar finite-velocity random motion with infinitely many possible directions. In this setting, we derive the distribution of the killed process and obtain an explicit representation of its density in terms of modified Bessel functions and a series involving Bessel polynomials.

entry.title: Uniform Asymptotic approximation and numerical evaluation of the Reverse Generalized Bessel Polynomial zeros
entry.summary: Uniform asymptotic expansions are derived for the zeros of the reverse generalized Bessel polynomials of large degree $n$ and real parameter $a$. It is assumed that $-Δ_{1} n+\frac{3}{2} \leq a \leq Δ_{2} n$ for fixed arbitrary $Δ_{1} \in (0,1)$ and bounded positive $Δ_{2}$. For this parameter range at most one of the zeros is real, with the rest being complex conjugates. The new expansions are uniformly valid for all the zeros, and are shown to be highly accurate for moderate or large values of $n$. They are consequently used as initial values in a very efficient numerical algorithm designed to obtain the remaining complex zeros using Taylor series.

entry.title: Simplified Airy function Asymptotic expansions for Reverse Generalised Bessel Polynomials
entry.summary: Uniform asymptotic expansions are derived for reverse generalised Bessel polynomials of large degree $n$, real parameter $a$, and complex argument $z$, which are simpler than previously known results. The defining differential equation is analysed; for large $n$ and $\frac{3}{2} - n < a < \infty$, it possesses two turning points in the complex $z$ plane which are complex conjugates. Away from these turning points Liouville-Green expansions are obtained for the polynomials and two companion solutions of the differential equation, where asymptotic series appear in the exponent. Then representations involving Airy functions and two slowly varying coefficient functions are constructed. Using the Liouville-Green representations, asymptotic expansions are obtained for the coefficient functions that involve coefficients that can be easily and explicitly computed recursively. In conjunction with a suitable re-expansion, or Cauchy's integral formula, near the turning point, the expansions are valid for $-Δ_{1} n+\frac{3}{2} \leq a \leq Δ_{2} n$ for fixed arbitrary $Δ_{1} \in (0,1)$ and bounded positive $Δ_{2}$, uniformly for all unbounded complex values of $z$.

entry.title: An Alternative Generating Function for $k$-Regular Partitions
entry.summary: We construct a $k$-fold $q$-series as a generating function of $k$-regular partitions for each positive integer $k$. The $k=1$ case is one of Euler's $q$-series identities pertaining to the partitions into distinct parts. The construction is combinatorial. Although we find a connection to Bessel polynomials in the $k=2$ case, this note is certainly not a study of Bessel polynomials and their $q$-analogs.

entry.title: Accurate algorithms for Bessel matrices
entry.summary: In this paper, we prove that any collocation matrix of Bessel polynomials at positive points is strictly totally positive, that is, all its minors are positive. Moreover, an accurate method to construct the bidiagonal factorization of these matrices is obtained and used to compute with high relative accuracy the eigenvalues, singular values and inverses. Similar results for the collocation matrices for the reverse Bessel polynomials are also obtained. Numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results are included.
